target.statement: BERT+SIK achieves AUROC 0.9414 on the BBC_News dataset, competitive with the best baselines (Table 3), demonstrating that the Simplified Isolation Kernel preserves detection performance with a low-dimensional sparse map.
target.table_ref: Table 3 (Evaluation results across 7 datasets in terms of AUROC), column BBC_News, row BERT+SIK
target.dataset: BBC_News (from NLP-ADBench; 1785 samples, 62 anomalies, 3.47% anomaly ratio)

compute.basis: SIK itself is a cheap CPU hypersphere-partitioning detector (seconds of runtime on ~1.8k points); the dominant cost is obtaining BERT embeddings for the BBC_News texts (either downloaded from NLP-ADBench or recomputed on CPU), plus a 5-run AUROC loop and hyperparameter search over psi.

blockers: Precomputed BERT embeddings for BBC_News may not be directly bundled; they may need to be regenerated (bert-base runs fine on CPU for ~1.8k short docs).
Reproducing the OpenAI/text-embedding-3-large rows (e.g. the bold 0.9844) would require a paid closed-source embedding API; the BERT-based cell avoids this.
title: Text Anomaly Detection with Simplified Isolation Kernel
